Which factor has the correct factor reward identified?
factor factor reward

A student has nothing to do on a Friday evening. She withdraws $5 from the $100 she has in a
savings account and buys a present to take to a party, to which admission is free.
What does this involve?

options.text: an opportunity cost equal to other goods she could have bought for $5
no opportunity cost, as entrance to the party is free
no opportunity cost, as she had no better way of using the time

questions.questionText: What would cause a shift in a country’s production possibility curve?

options.text: the destruction of factories in a war

questions.questionText: Which topic is studied in macroeconomics?

China is moving towards a more mixed economic system and reducing the role of the public
sector.
Which economic policy measure might best achieve this?

options.text: creating excess capacity in state-owned enterprises
encouraging competition among private sector firms

questions.questionText: Which statement about price elasticity of demand (PED) is correct?

options.text: PED measures the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price.
PED measures the change in price divided by the change in the quantity demanded.
PED means a change in price will cause an equal change in the quantity demanded.
PED means a change in demand will result in a greater percentage change in price.

A manufacturer of tinned beans mechanises its assembly line. This increases output by 30% and
reduces labour by 20%.
How and why will this affect supply curve S?
price of
tinned
beans
quantity of
tinned beans

options.text: S will move to the left due to an increase in average costs.
S will move to the left due to an increase in the price of tinned beans.
S will move to the right due to an increase in consumer demand.
S will move to the right due to an increase in productivity.

Suppliers have decided to produce 10000 units and charge a price of $6.
What is the result of this decision in the short run?

options.text: A stable equilibrium price will be achieved.
Suppliers will be left with unsold stock.
The equilibrium market price will increase.
There will be excess demand at the price of $6.

questions.questionText:
A cinema has 500 seats. It raised its admission price from $2 to $5 and daily revenue increased
from $800 to $1500.
What can be concluded from this information?

options.text: Price elasticity of demand for cinema seats was elastic.
Price elasticity of supply of cinema seats was elastic.
The cinema operated below full capacity.

questions.questionText: What is an outcome of a competitive market?
What might prevent an individual choosing a particular occupation?

options.text: low cost of travelling to work
wage rate above national minimum wage

questions.questionText: What might encourage a consumer to spend less and save more?

options.text: the expectation that prices will fall
the expectation that prices will rise
the expectation that unemployment will fall
the expectation that real GDP will rise

Which activity is correctly linked to the organisation that provides it?
organisation activity

options.text: central bank regulate the rate of inflation
central bank set direct tax rates
commercial bank manage the government’s financial accounts
commercial bank safeguard the country’s foreign reserves

questions.questionText: What is not usually a macroeconomic aim?

A government decides to increase the indirect tax on petrol. Petrol has an inelastic price elasticity
of demand.
What are likely to be the consequences?
quantity of government
petrol bought revenue

In a country, there is an increase in the rate of interest to prevent inflation.
Which type of macroeconomic policy is this?

A government significantly increases its spending on education and training over several years.
What will be the likely effect of this policy measure on the rate of inflation in both the short run
and the long run?
short-run effect long-run effect
What may cause a recession?
Why might the macroeconomic aim of full employment conflict with the aim of stable prices?

options.text: Full employment leads to higher cost of imports.
Full employment leads to increased income inequality.
Full employment leads to increases in wages.
Full employment leads to lower exports.

questions.questionText:
In a country, inflation is 10% and nominal interest rates are 7%.
Which group is most likely to benefit from this situation?
Which action is not performed by a government as part of its international role?

Which components, in addition to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per head, are included in the
Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: average earnings and inequalities of incomes
balance of trade and balance of payments
life expectancy at birth and expected years of schooling
size of population and age structure of population

questions.questionText: What is likely to cause an immediate decrease in the size of the labour force?

options.text: a fall in the average size of families
a fall in the birth rate
a reduction in the age of retirement

questions.questionText:
The table shows some economic indicators.
Which increase in the first indicator is most likely to lead to an increase in the second indicator?
first indicator second indicator
When are countries most likely to specialise and trade with each other?

options.text: when the cost of transport between them is high
when there are large differences in their resource allocations
when they have access to the same technology
when they have high tariffs and other protective measures

questions.questionText:
A government removed the quota on goods imported into the country.
What is the most likely result of this?

options.text: a decrease in demand for domestic production
a decrease in the balance of trade deficit

questions.questionText:
A country has a surplus on the current account of its balance of payments.
What would be most likely to cause the country to move into deficit?

options.text: devaluation of its fixed exchange rate
productivity increases in its export industries

questions.questionText:
The governments of low-income countries often allow foreign multinational companies (MNCs) to
mine minerals in their country.
Which conflict between benefit and cost might this cause the low-income countries?
benefit cost

options.text: improved balance of trade training by the MNCs
higher employment loss of a finite resource
increased profits for the MNCs efficient production
